# Known Limitations

1. **No accessible v0.1 source package was found.** The build continues the approved architecture and safety boundaries found in the Manuel Academy project materials, but it cannot perform a file-by-file merge against an unavailable v0.1 archive.
2. **Demonstration content only.** The math and English interactions prove the engine contract; subject owners must create and validate final curriculum packages.
3. **No provider integration.** Prompt templates are included, but no OpenAI, Anthropic, ElevenLabs, or other provider is called.
4. **Browser speech varies.** Speech quality, voices, and availability depend on the local browser and operating system. Captions and transcript are the authoritative fallback.
5. **Rule-based safety matching is incomplete.** Production safety requires an approved server-side policy, durable adult review path, and comprehensive evaluation.
6. **Confidence is instructional, not psychometric.** The model is transparent and conservative but has not been calibrated as a standardized assessment instrument.
7. **No high-stakes decisions.** The engine cannot determine grade placement, disability eligibility, promotion, retention, or formal mastery certification.
8. **No persistence.** Refreshing the page resets the session. This is intentional until authenticated progress synchronization is separately approved.
9. **No real media assets.** The visual board uses CSS and DOM primitives. Missing-media fallbacks are implemented; external image/video generation is out of scope.
10. **Sequencing UI not demonstrated.** The sequencing assessment contract and evaluator exist, but the browser prototype’s two fixtures use multiple-choice items.
11. **English free-response scoring is bounded.** The core supports exact normalized short answers; production paragraph revision needs a separately evaluated rubric and provider policy.
12. **No localization package.** Contracts support locale metadata, but only en-US demonstration text is included.
